pattern.top_pattern: Authorized acute hospital spend is surging in MO and recurring in other TANF Standard markets
pattern.what_is_impacting: Medicaid / TANF Standard / ACUTE HOSPITAL prior-authorization admissions
key_driver_codes: Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
Major Small and Large Bowel Procedures with CC
Cranial and Peripheral Nerve Disorders without MCC
pattern.pattern_details: MO is the dominant driver of authorized acute hospital spend growth, and the increase is not purely a volume story. Admissions rose materially and paid per admission also increased, with additional recurring pressure in CA, FL, KS, MD, OH, NC, LA, and NY. The pattern shows broad inpatient pressure in TANF Standard rather than a single isolated case.
pattern.why_it_matters: This is the largest operational cost pattern and points to combined utilization management and reimbursement pressure in a core Medicaid inpatient setting.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Launch a joint UM and reimbursement review for TANF Standard acute hospital admissions, starting in MO, with focused review of postpartum, pneumothorax, bowel, and nerve disorder stays where both admission counts and cost per stay increased.
evidence_summary: MO TANF Standard acute hospital claims increased about $28.6M, with 887 more admissions and about $1.4K higher paid per admission.
A broader CA, FL, KS, MD, and OH acute hospital group added about $3.9M, showing the pattern is recurring outside MO.
CA also had a separate volume-led increase of about $1.9M in TANF Standard acute hospital admissions, including 66 more admissions in major bowel procedures.
NC and LA/NY added roughly $1.0M combined, again led by higher authorized inpatient volume.
